query: Consider the following context: High-entropy alloy (HEA) multilayers represent a promising class of advanced coating materials due to their superior mechanical properties, corrosion resistance, and irradiation tolerance. However, the specific role of interface coherency on the creep behavior of HEA multilayers remains unclear. In that context, which material can be used for transition between diffusion-mediated and dislocation-mediated creep mechanisms, and why?

generation.hypothesis: In CoCrFeNiMn-based high-entropy alloy (HEA) multilayers, increasing interface mismatch (i.e., reducing coherency) will shift the dominant creep mechanism from diffusion-controlled to dislocation-controlled processes at intermediate temperatures and stresses.
generation.material_initial_state: A CoCrFeNiMn HEA multilayer with coherent interfaces deposited at room temperature, exhibiting a single fcc solid-solution without significant phase segregation.
generation.intervention: Systematically vary the lattice mismatch between adjacent layers (e.g., via doping or adjusting composition) to generate a gradient from coherent to semi-coherent/incoherent interfaces.
generation.conditions: Intermediate temperature range (e.g., 500–600 °C) under different applied stress levels to explore transitions between creep regimes.
generation.structural_mediator: Coherence or incoherence of the interlayer interfaces in the CoCrFeNiMn multilayer system.
generation.mechanism: Coherent interfaces enhance diffusion-based creep by promoting diffusion pathways, while semi-coherent or incoherent interfaces will facilitate dislocation motion and shift the dominant creep mechanism toward dislocation-mediated processes.
generation.predicted_outcome: At lower stresses (and more coherent interfaces), the creep exponent will drop (approximately 5–6), indicating diffusion-mediated processes. At higher stresses or with incoherent interfaces, the creep exponent will increase (~8–15), indicating dislocation-based mechanisms.
generation.baseline: A single-phase CoCrFeNiMn HEA with fully coherent interfaces and known diffusion-limited creep response under similar temperature–stress conditions.
generation.boundary: This effect may be diminished or masked at temperatures well above 600 °C, where additional recovery processes or dynamic recrystallization become significant, or at very low stresses where creep strains are too small to detect or isolate interface effects.
generation.uncertainty: The degree of interface mismatch necessary to induce a clear transition remains unquantified without dedicated experimentation; the precise effect may also depend on potential short-range order.

falsification_experiment.design: Deposit a series of CoCrFeNiMn HEA multilayers by magnetron sputtering with graded composition changes at the layer interfaces to control interfacial mismatch. Perform uniaxial creep tests under varying stress levels at 500–600 °C in an in-situ TEM or synchrotron setup to track dislocation activities and measure strain rates.
measurements: Microscopic examination of interface structure and coherence (TEM, diffraction, XRD).
Creep deformation rates under systematically varied stress and temperature.
Characterization of dislocation activity and substructure evolution in real time.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If varying interface mismatch does not induce distinct changes in the creep exponent or the relative contributions of diffusion versus dislocation-mediated deformation, then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: High-entropy alloys (HEAs), as a novel type of material generally consisting of five or more principle elements, have attracted extensive attention in recent years because of their attractive crystallographic and mechanical properties [ [1] , [2] , [3] , [4] , [5] , [6] , [7] ]. Although it is anticipated that simple solid solution phases are easier to form rather than the intermetallic compounds or complex-ordered phases due to their high configurational entropy [ [8] , [9] ], only a few HEAs have exactly single and stable solid solution structures, among which CoCrFeNiMn alloy is widely concerned [ [10] , [11] , [12] , [13] , [14] ]. It possesses a single face-center-cubic (fcc) solid solution phase even after a series of thermomechanical processing [ [15] , [16] ] and its constituent elements have more sluggish diffusion compared to other conventional alloys [ [17] ]. These characterizations contribute to excellent mechanical properties with a satisfactory combination between tensile strength and ductility [ [18] , [19] ]. decision.trend: A single study on equiatomic CoCrFeNiMn high-entropy alloy (PMC7512559) has systematically examined transition regions in creep by varying stress at intermediate temperatures (500–600 °C). Researchers observed a lower-stress regime suggesting stress-assisted diffusion-mediated dislocation climb (stress exponent ~5–6) and a higher-stress regime exhibiting elevated exponents (8.9–14) with dynamic recrystallization. Although it clarifies the transition from diffusion control to dislocation-dominated mechanisms, it does not address how interface coherency in multilayers could shift or tune that transition.
decision.unsolved: How coherent vs. incoherent interfaces in HEA multilayers may modify the transition from diffusion-mediated to dislocation-mediated creep remains unclear, and systematic experiments on interface-controlled creep mechanisms are lacking.
decision.lever: Use in-situ TEM or synchrotron-based creep tests on CoCrFeNiMn-based multilayers with systematically varied interface mismatch to capture the real-time evolution of dislocation and diffusion processes across coherent vs. incoherent interfaces.
decision.why: CoCrFeNiMn is a known benchmark for investigating transitions between diffusion-based and dislocation-dominant creep, as demonstrated by stress-dependent creep regimes. Directly monitoring interface deformation via in-situ techniques will reveal how coherency influences creep pathways in HEA multilayer coatings, addressing the remaining gap about interface effects.
